stories.title: Chinese humanoid robots smash human records in 100m sprint and high jump at Beijing robot games
stories.summary:
Chinese humanoid robots broke human athletic records on the opening day of the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. The event, described as an Olympics-like competition for robotics, featured several record-setting performances.

One robot completed a 100-meter sprint in 9.39 seconds, surpassing Usain Bolt's long-standing world record. This achievement was highlighted by multiple news outlets covering the opening heat of the games.

In addition to the sprint, Chinese robots also set new marks in high jump. The demonstrations showcased rapid advancements in humanoid robotics and their increasing capability in physical athletic events.

stories.title: Court sides with conservative activist James O’Keefe in First Amendment case
stories.summary:
A federal appeals court in Washington, D.C., has overturned a $130,000 jury verdict against conservative activist James O’Keefe. The ruling resolves a legal dispute stemming from undercover video clips published during the 2016 presidential election.

The case involved Democratic consultant Robert Creamer and his businesses, who had won damages in a lower court decision in 2022. The appeals court determined that the original jury award violated First Amendment protections related to O’Keefe’s publication of the footage.

O’Keefe, founder and former CEO of Project Veritas, had appealed the initial judgment after publishing clips that depicted violence outside Donald Trump campaign rallies. The appellate decision effectively clears him of the financial liability previously imposed by the jury.

stories.title: US-Canada trade deal collapses as Trump’s 50% tariffs go into effect
stories.summary:
A last-minute U.S.-Canada trade agreement collapsed just before President Donald Trump’s Friday night deadline, allowing the administration’s 50% tariffs on Canadian goods to take effect overnight. The breakdown ended a final round of negotiations that had sought to ease tensions between the two historic allies.

The new measures will impose a 50% tariff on roughly $28 billion in Canadian products imported into the United States, according to the Washington Examiner. Canada said it would immediately retaliate against the move, signaling a sharp escalation in trade relations.

stories.title: Seven First Nations Australians tell us their worries and hopes for future generations – video
stories.summary:
Seven First Nations Australians share their worries and hopes for future generations in a new video from The Guardian Australia.

The piece highlights East Arnhem Land, described as one of the last strongholds of Aboriginal culture in Australia. It is home to the Yolngu people, who maintain one of the oldest continuous cultures on Earth.

The land is fully owned and managed by traditional owners under inalienable Aboriginal freehold title, meaning it can never be bought or sold.

Each year, the Yolngu host the Garma festival, described as Australia's largest Indigenous political and cultural gathering. The event brings together First Nations leaders from around the country.

stories.summary:
Timothy Garton Ash argues that artificial intelligence is advancing faster than humanity's ability to control it. He notes that experts in Silicon Valley expect an extraordinary AI takeoff within the next couple of years.

The imminent breakthrough is described as recursive self-improvement, a point at which systems can enhance their own capabilities. Some observers refer to this period as the foothills of the singularity.

Ash questions whether even a catastrophic AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima would be enough to make humankind protect itself. He expresses fear that humanity may not respond adequately to such existential risks.

stories.title: Will AI give you the job? Automated hiring tools spark discrimination and secrecy lawsuits
stories.summary:
A growing number of lawsuits are challenging the use of artificial intelligence in employment decisions, raising fresh questions about how companies hire and fire. The legal disputes center on automated hiring tools that applicants say have contributed to discrimination and opaque decision-making.

The Guardian reports that Erin Kistler, a product manager with nearly four years of job applications behind her, has sent résumés to major employers including PayPal, Microsoft, and Netflix without meaningful response. Her experience is cited as an example of candidates feeling lost in what she describes as a black hole of automated screening.

The lawsuits suggest that the opacity of AI-driven hiring systems may be creating legal exposure for employers. As more workers and job seekers bring claims to court, companies are being pushed to explain how these tools evaluate applicants and whether they comply with anti-discrimination laws.
